content: The following are the adverse effects associated with the use of Vytorin, which contains ezetimibe and simvastatin, as reported in clinical trials and post-marketing experience: Adverse Effects of Ezetimibe (from placebo-controlled studies): 1. General Disorders: Fatigue. 2. Gastrointestinal Disorders: Abdominal pain, diarrhea. 3. Infections and Infestations: Viral infections, pharyngitis, sinusitis. 4. Musculoskeletal Disorders: Joint pain (arthralgia), back pain. 5. Respiratory Disorders: Coughing. Post-Marketing Adverse Reactions for Ezetimibe: 1. Hypersensitivity Reactions: These include anaphylaxis, angioedema, rash, and urticaria. 2. Musculoskeletal Disorders: Joint pain (arthralgia), muscle pain (myalgia). 3. Hepatic Effects: Elevated liver transaminases, hepatitis. 4. Hematologic Effects: Thrombocytopenia. 5. Pancreatic Effects: Pancreatitis. 6. Neurological Effects: Dizziness, paresthesia. 7. Psychiatric Effects: Depression. 8. Gallbladder Disorders: Gallstones (cholelithiasis), inflammation of the gallbladder (cholecystitis). 9. Other Rare Effects: Elevated creatine phosphokinase levels, and very rarely, myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Adverse Effects of Simvastatin (from placebo-controlled studies): 1. General Disorders: Weakness (asthenia). 2. Eye Disorders: Cataracts. 3. Gastrointestinal Disorders: Abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, indigestion (dyspepsia), flatulence, nausea. 4. Skin Disorders: Eczema, itching (pruritus), rash. Additional Adverse Effects Reported with HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors (Statins, including Simvastatin): 1. Musculoskeletal Disorders: Muscle cramps, muscle pain (myalgia), myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, joint pain (arthralgia). 2. Nervous System Disorders: Dysfunction of cranial nerves (e.g., altered taste, impaired eye movement, facial weakness), tremor, dizziness, memory loss, paresthesia, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral nerve palsy, and psychiatric disturbances. 3. Ear Disorders: Vertigo. 4. Psychiatric Disorders: Anxiety, insomnia, depression, decreased libido. 5. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Rare hypersensitivity syndrome, which may include anaphylaxis, angioedema, lupus-like syndrome, polymyalgia rheumatica, dermatomyositis, vasculitis, purpura, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, positive ANA, increased ESR, eosinophilia, arthritis, joint pain (arthralgia), urticaria, weakness (asthenia), photosensitivity, fever, chills, flushing, malaise, shortness of breath (dyspnea), toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome. 6. Gastrointestinal Disorders: Pancreatitis, vomiting. 7. Hepatobiliary Disorders: Hepatitis (including chronic active hepatitis), cholestatic jaundice, fatty liver changes, and rarely, cirrhosis, fulminant hepatic necrosis, hepatic failure, and hepatoma. 8. Metabolic Disorders: Anorexia. 9. Skin Disorders: Hair loss (alopecia), itching (pruritus), skin nodules, discoloration, dryness of skin or mucous membranes, and changes in hair or nails. 10. Reproductive Disorders: Gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction. 11. Eye Disorders: Progression of cataracts (lens opacities), ophthalmoplegia. 12. Laboratory Abnormalities: Elevated transaminases, alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, and bilirubin; thyroid function abnormalities. Laboratory Test Abnormalities: 1. Persistent elevations in serum transaminases have been observed. 2. Approximately 5% of patients taking simvastatin experienced elevations in creatine kinase (CK) levels to three or more times the normal value on one or more occasions. These elevations were attributed to the non-cardiac fraction of CK. Muscle pain or dysfunction was generally not reported. Concomitant Lipid-Lowering Therapy: In controlled clinical studies where simvastatin was administered alongside cholestyramine, no unique adverse reactions specific to this combination were observed. The adverse reactions reported were consistent with those previously associated with simvastatin or cholestyramine. Adolescent Patients (Ages 10–17): In a 48-week controlled study involving adolescent boys and post-menarcheal girls (ages 10–17) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, the safety and tolerability profile of simvastatin (10–40 mg daily) was generally similar to that of the placebo group. The most common adverse experiences in both groups included upper respiratory infections, headache, abdominal pain, and nausea.
